summary: Builds: taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean exits 0 (5.2 s). There are exactly two 'declaration uses sorry' warnings, at l.788 (absGal_Y₂_fiber_not_compact) and l.836 (wild_cantor_not_isSLSCIn), which matches REPORT sorry_count 2. #print axioms was run from a /tmp file, so nothing was written to the repo. It is clean (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) for following_situations_finite, _finite_euclidean, _tame, _tame_knot, _simplicial, _simplicial_false, absGal_not_isSLSCIn, printedGamma2_eq_top and not_isSLSCIn_of_essential. sorryAx appears only under absGal_Y₂_fiber_not_cantor, as reported. Exactly the three labels of l.1560-1583 are present and none is bold-marked, which fits the unruled homotopy reading of 'almost trivial'. No declaration name clashes with GX/ or scaffold/: all 64 top-level names were grepped. Items 1 and 2 are sound and at least as strong as the paper under the disclosed readings. The absGal first claim is proved soundly (essential-loop criterion, p = 1/(2k+3) so the loop misses S). The printed-Gamma2 finding is correct. The non-compactness refutation is stated under a sorry. Its D_inf sketch is robust: any loop whose winding class is a_n maps to a reflection, so Gamma2 is killed for every admissible gamma, not only for simple loops. The sorry'd statement is therefore plausibly true and the sorry is a genuine obstruction. BLOCKER: wild_cantor_not_isSLSCIn is stated for EVERY wild Cantor set, and that statement is false. Wild Cantor sets in S^3 with simply connected complement exist (Kirkor; Skora, Topology Appl. 24 (1986) 181-188; rigid examples of Garity-Repovs-Zeljko, PAMS 2006). For such a C, C^c IS semi-locally simply connected in S^3 under the file's own IsSLSCIn. Take a loop of Omega(x,x,C^c) and cut off short end arcs. Their endpoints lie in a small ball B minus C, which is path-connected because a 0-dimensional closed set does not separate an open set of a 3-manifold. The middle piece is then homotopic rel endpoints in the simply connected C^c to a path inside B minus C. So the paper's 'wild' needs the cited Blankinship/Antoine necklace class, and the row must be corrected under DEC-27, not stated with a sorry. MAJOR: the counterexample to item 3 (triangle plus an isolated vertex) is disconnected. It therefore falls outside the standing hypothesis 'X connected' of def:semi_locally_simple_connectedness (l.1451), which REPORT itself lists. A connected counterexample exists (n = 3: a tetrahedron with a dangling edge, where the free edge is a maximal 1-face inside the 1-skeleton) and must replace it. Minor issues: purity is stronger than the true condition; the docstring says ℝ³ where the code uses ℝ⁴; the locally-finite and subspace-topology restriction is not justified in the findings.

issues.where: GX.wild_cantor_not_isSLSCIn (l.836) with GX.IsWildCantor (l.817); REPORT row ex:wild_cantor_general_antoine
issues.problem: The stated theorem, 'every wild Cantor set C of S^3 has C^c not semi-locally simply connected in S^3', is false, so the tagged sorry hides a false statement rather than an obstruction. Wild Cantor sets in S^3 with simply connected complement exist: Kirkor; R. Skora, 'Cantor sets in S^3 with simply connected complements', Topology Appl. 24 (1986) 181-188; Garity-Repovs-Zeljko, 'Rigid Cantor sets in R^3 with simply connected complement', PAMS 134 (2006). Rigid implies wild, and S^3 = R^3 plus a point keeps the complement simply connected. For such C, IsSLSCIn C^c holds. (i) Density: C has empty interior. (ii) At x in C, take V = S^3. Given gamma in Omega(x,x,C^c) and a neighbourhood W of x, pick a ball B inside W around x. B minus C is path-connected, because a closed 0-dimensional set does not separate a connected open subset of a 3-manifold. Choose eps with gamma([0,eps] and [1-eps,1]) inside B, and sigma a path in B minus C from gamma(eps) to gamma(1-eps). Then gamma restricted to [eps,1-eps] is homotopic to sigma rel endpoints in the simply connected C^c. Concatenating with the end arcs gives an OmegaHomotopic C^c homotopy from gamma to a loop of Omega(x,x,W cap C^c). (iii) At x not in C: C^c is an open 3-manifold, so it is locally simply connected. REPORT's finding ('the claim for an arbitrary wild Cantor set rests on Bing's tameness criterion ... and on passing from a failure of 1-ULC to loops based at a point of S') misdiagnoses this: no such passage exists in general. The paper's citation general_antoine is Blankinship 1951, 'Generalization of a construction of Antoine', which points to the necklace class, not to all wild Cantor sets.
issues.fix: Apply DEC-27. (1) Restate the positive claim in its strongest true form. Either use Antoine's necklace, or Blankinship's generalized necklaces, constructed explicitly in S^3. Or use the abstract form: some x in C has, in every neighbourhood, a loop essential in the complement of a compact piece of C away from x. In the abstract form the conclusion is already GX.not_isSLSCIn_of_essential. Keep a tagged sorry only on the genuine Antoine pi_1 obstruction. (2) Prove the general half that refutes the literal reading: if C is closed, nowhere separating in small balls (or 0-dimensional) and C^c is simply connected, then IsSLSCIn C^c. This is provable with the API of Paths.lean. (3) Record the finding that l.1578 is false for wild Cantor sets with simply connected complement (Kirkor/Skora), with the existence of those sets as the cited, unformalized input. (4) Set the row to partial and correct the REPORT finding.

issues.where: GX.following_situations_simplicial_false and GX.cexK (l.454-559); REPORT finding for l.1564
issues.problem: The counterexample for item 3 is a triangle together with an isolated vertex, so |K| is DISCONNECTED. The paper's def:semi_locally_simple_connectedness (l.1451) works in a Hausdorff, CONNECTED, locally path-connected space, and REPORT lists '§3 standing: Y Hausdorff, connected, LPC' as a hypothesis of the row. The counterexample therefore refutes the Lean IsSLSCIn form but not the paper's item 3 inside its own setting. With n = 2 no connected counterexample exists: a maximal face of dimension 0 is an isolated vertex. The finding 'false as written' is nonetheless TRUE in the connected setting. For n = 3, take a tetrahedron with an edge attached at a vertex. The free edge is a maximal face of dimension 1 = n-2, it lies in the 1-skeleton, and Y minus S misses a neighbourhood of its interior points, so Y minus S is not dense. That is the counterexample DEC-27 requires.
issues.fix: Replace or supplement the counterexample with a connected one. For example, in Fin 5 -> R (or Fin 6 -> R), take the faces of a tetrahedron {e0,e1,e2,e3} plus the edge {e3,e4} with n = 3, and prove that K.space is connected (or path-connected) together with non-density. Update the finding and the SCOPE (c) text to match.

issues.where: GX.IsPureDim (l.347) as the hypothesis of GX.following_situations_simplicial (l.442)
issues.problem: Purity is sufficient but not the strongest true form. Y minus S is dense exactly when every face lies in a face of dimension at least n-1, that is, with at least n vertices. A 2-complex made of a triangle with a dangling edge is not pure, yet item 3 holds for it. REPORT's own finding names the correct condition ('a face of dimension <= n-2 which is maximal') but the theorem assumes more.
issues.fix: Weaken IsPureDim K n to 'every face lies in a face with card >= n'. The proof of dense_compl_skeleton goes through unchanged: rho cap tau is still a proper face of tau, because card rho <= n-1 < card tau. Alternatively, add this as a second theorem.

issues.problem: The docstring says the counterexample is 'a triangle and an isolated vertex in ℝ³', but the code (cexK, over Fin 4 -> ℝ) and REPORT both say ℝ⁴.
issues.fix: Change ℝ³ to ℝ⁴, or to whatever ambient space the connected replacement uses.

issues.where: following_situations_simplicial: LocallyFinite hypothesis; REPORT hypotheses row for item 3
issues.problem: The restriction to locally finite geometric complexes with the subspace topology is inherited from rem:simple_cases (WP-26f) and listed as 'strengthened'. It is neither a finding nor a question, and its justification is not stated. That justification is that for a locally finite complex the subspace topology is the paper's (weak) simplicial topology, while mathlib has no weak topology.
issues.fix: Add one sentence to SCOPE (c) and REPORT recording why local finiteness is the modelling choice. Raise a question if the master session wants the non-locally-finite (weak topology) case.

questions_for_author: l.1578: is the 'wild Cantor set' of ex:wild_cantor_general_antoine meant to be Antoine's or Blankinship's necklace (the cited class)? For arbitrary wild Cantor sets the claim is false: wild Cantor sets with simply connected complement (Kirkor, Skora 1986) have a semi-locally simply connected complement in the sense of l.1451.

l.1572: is Gamma2 meant to be the normal closure of the squares [gamma_n]^2? The printed double cosets give all of Gamma. If so, is the Cantor-fibre claim meant for an abelian quotient instead (the kernel of the mod-2 winding numbers)? With the normal closure the fibre over 0 surjects onto an infinite discrete coset space via a D_inf quotient, so it is not compact.

Still pending from WP-26e/26f: the homotopy reading of 'almost trivial' (AlmostTrivial against the compact-open AlmostTrivialCC). No row of this file can be marked until it is ruled, and the negative result absGal_not_isSLSCIn is proved only under it.
